key_insight: Dynamic transformation of 1-acetylpiperazine (PX) couples crystallization control with interface passivation in lead-free tin-based perovskite solar cells.
engineering_relevance: A single additive addresses both film growth and interfacial defects, offering a route to more efficient and stable lead-free photovoltaics.
method: PX carbonyl groups coordinate with Sn²⁺ to stabilize precursor complexes and moderate supersaturation.
Controlled crystal growth produces compact, highly crystalline perovskite films.
Annealing is proposed to form amidinium-functionalized species that passivate surface A-site vacancies.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 15.18% power conversion efficiency and retention of 94.1% of initial efficiency after 500 hours of continuous illumination.
watch_item: The proposed molecular transformation requires further confirmation, and the abstract does not specify device area or stability-test conditions.
paper_title: Dynamic Molecular Transformation Mediated Crystallization Regulation and Interface Passivation in Tin Based Perovskite Solar Cells
